title: FlipGFP protease assay for evaluating inhibitory activity against SARS-CoV-2 Mpro and PLpro
author: Tan, Hu, et al.

steps.title: Seed and assess HEK293T cells
steps.instruction: Seed HEK293T cells in a T75 flask. On the second day after seeding, examine the culture under a phase‑contrast inverted microscope and confirm that the monolayer has reached 70–80 % confluence, which gives the most efficient transfection.

steps.title: Dilute plasmids to 500 ng/µL
steps.instruction: Dilute the FlipGFP reporter plasmid and the protease plasmid with autoclaved nuclease‑free water to a concentration of 500 ng/µL each.

steps.title: Prepare transfection complexes
steps.instruction: For each well of a 96‑well plate, mix the following on ice (or at room temperature): 9 µL Opti‑MEM, 0.1 µL of the 500 ng/µL reporter plasmid, 0.1 µL of the 500 ng/µL protease plasmid, and 0.3 µL transIT‑293 reagent. Prepare a master mix if multiple wells are to be transfected.

steps.title: Incubate transfection mix
steps.instruction: Gently vortex the transfection mixture and let it sit at room temperature for 30 min.

steps.title: Add transfection mix to cells
steps.instruction: Add 9.5 µL of the transfection complex to each well of the 96‑well plate, delivering 50 ng of reporter plasmid and 50 ng of protease plasmid per well.

steps.title: Mix complexes in wells
steps.instruction: Place the plate on a shaker and mix the contents of each well for 5 min.

steps.title: Incubate for expression
steps.instruction: Transfer the plate to a humidified cell‑culture incubator set to 5 % CO₂/95 % air at 37 °C and incubate for 3 h to allow transfection and protein expression.

steps.title: Include assay controls
steps.instruction: In parallel, set up control wells: (i) matching protease‑FlipGFP pairs, (ii) mismatching pairs, (iii) positive‑control inhibitor (potent, non‑cytotoxic) at multiple concentrations, and (iv) negative‑control compound (inactive, non‑cytotoxic). Ensure that mCherry fluorescence remains constant across control wells to confirm successful transfection and to monitor cytotoxicity.

steps.title: Measure GFP and mCherry fluorescence
steps.instruction: After the expression period, read the fluorescence of each well using a plate reader (appropriate excitation/emission settings for GFP and mCherry). Record the raw GFP and mCherry values for every concentration of each test compound. The raw data as presented in the original article are:

steps.title: Calculate GFP/mCherry ratios
steps.instruction: For each well, divide the GFP fluorescence value by the corresponding mCherry fluorescence value to obtain the GFP/mCherry ratio.

steps.title: Normalize GFP/mCherry for EC50
steps.instruction: Define the GFP/mCherry ratio of the DMSO‑treated group as 100 %. Define the GFP/mCherry ratio of the control compound at its highest tested concentration (60 µM) as 0 % (cut‑off). Apply this linear normalization to all test‑compound ratios before curve fitting.

steps.title: Normalize mCherry for CC50
steps.instruction: Define the mCherry fluorescence of the DMSO‑treated group as 100 % and the mCherry signal of the non‑transfected wells as 0 %. Normalize all mCherry values accordingly before generating cytotoxicity curves.

steps.title: Create dose‑response curves in GraphPad Prism
steps.instruction: Open GraphPad Prism 8 and select ‘New table & graph’. Choose ‘XY’ as the graph type. Enter three replicates for the Y‑values (GFP/mCherry ratios) at each concentration. Convert compound concentrations to log‑scale and place them in column X. Input the normalized GFP/mCherry values for each replicate in column Y. Click ‘Analyze’, choose ‘Normalize’, set 0 % to the mean of the 60 µM control‑compound group and 100 % to the mean of the DMSO group. Then run a nonlinear regression fit using ‘log (inhibitor) vs. response – variable slope’. Record the EC₅₀ values. For cytotoxicity, repeat the same steps using the normalized mCherry values to obtain CC₅₀ values.

steps.title: Interpret results and handle cytotoxicity
steps.instruction: If a test compound shows a decrease in mCherry signal at high concentrations (indicating cytotoxicity), discard the GFP/mCherry ratios at those toxic concentrations and re‑plot the dose‑response using only the non‑toxic data points. Report EC₅₀ values for enzymatic inhibition and CC₅₀ values for cytotoxicity.
